blocks.html: Dealers absorb customer order imbalances while managing inventory risk and scarce balance-sheet capacity. Inventory affects optimal dealer pricing (Ho and Stoll, 1981), FX dealing (Lyons, 1995), and observed inventory adjustment in dealership markets (Hansch, Naik and Viswanathan, 1998). Treasury intermediation likewise depends on dealer capacity (Duffie et al., 2023). A forecast of the maximum recorded position magnitude over a future horizon may support monitoring of the measured position: an endpoint can return toward its starting value after an intervening large position. Translating that monitoring signal into a particular margin or financing decision requires the corresponding contractual and balance-sheet inputs.

We ask whether mature conditional estimators improve forecasts of an absolute sampled-position peak relative to simple historical constructions. Every procedure predicts the same upper quantile of the same response on common issue origins. The historical alternatives use past headrooms, paths translated to the current signed position, or native peaks floored at the observed current magnitude. The conditional alternatives use ridge quantile regression, nearest-neighbor quantiles and scaled nearest-neighbor quantiles.

The matched-history FX regression comparison lowers mean loss by 14.77%, but increases breaches from 360 to 376. The original FX primary uses a different historical window and lowers loss by 12.66%. The separately declared Treasury primary deteriorates by 50.79%, with 54 rather than 28 breaches. Short-history FX regression also deteriorates at the longer horizon; a Treasury neighbor gain reverses on the sparse grid. These adverse outcomes are central findings.

The paper makes three contributions. First, it places established forecasting engines and historical constructions on a common completed-peak response with an explicit issue-known floor. Second, it controls completed-label pools and update schedules and retains the complete favorable and adverse model menu. Third, it documents how score, breach frequency, report coherence and fixed-report preferences can disagree across two financial measurement processes. The contribution is an application and model-validation benchmark using mature methods.

Section 2 locates the study in the literature. Sections 3–5 describe data, forecasts and evaluation. Sections 6–7 report FX and Treasury results. Section 8 collects exploratory robustness evidence, Section 9 discusses mechanisms and limitations, and Section 10 concludes. Detailed historical menus, geometry and supplementary diagnostics appear in the appendices.

Wisniewski, Lindsay and Lindsay (2020) and the net-position forecasting chapter of Wisniewski (2024) are the closest empirical lineage. They already study conditional, neighbor and normalized endpoint forecasts on the FX source family, using lagged positions and calendar information. Here the response is a single upper quantile of a future absolute sampled maximum, including the current magnitude. Marginal endpoint intervals and their averaged losses address a different functional; the present comparison fits the established engines directly to completed peak labels.

Financial path extrema have a substantial prior literature. MaxVaR evaluates worst intermediate mark-to-market loss (Boudoukh et al., 2004). Liao and Theodosopoulos (2005) study the timing of mark-to-market for collateralized contingent credit exposure. Van den Hoogen (2017) models a conditional intraday liquidity buffer through the maximum cumulative payment deficit; Petrunia, Sabetti and Voia (2019) study a cross-participant end-of-day debit maximum. Arjani, Li and Sabetti (2020) forecast remaining-day liquidity-demand ratios. These targets clarify the specific contribution of a sampled net-position envelope.

Regression quantiles (Koenker and Bassett, 1978), sequential neighbor quantiles (Biau and Patra, 2011), conditional historical filtering (Hull and White, 1998; Barone-Adesi et al., 1999), and quantile scoring (Gneiting, 2011) supply the mature methods. Quantile forests (Meinshausen, 2006), CAViaR (Engle and Manganelli, 2004), sequential conformal prediction (Xu and Xie, 2023), trajectory calibration (Zhou, Lindemann and Sesia, 2024) and expected-shortfall curves (Sözen, 2026) are further relevant alternatives. The executed estimator menu is deliberately bounded.

The resulting distinction is the measured peak response, known issue floor, completed-label timing, controlled history/update comparisons and qualified aggregate application. The benchmark measures how these mature procedures behave on the specified task; its supporting finite geometry explains construction differences.

current_contribution_assessment.claim: Established forecasting engines on a completed peak/headroom response with an issue-known floor
current_contribution_assessment.reason: A peak depends on the joint future path and differs from a signed endpoint interval; direct fitting to this response creates a meaningful benchmark. Known-floor projection and translating headroom are elementary operations, not new estimator primitives. Financial peak quantiles and liquidity buffers already have prior examples; priority for the exact source/target combination is unproved.

current_contribution_assessment.claim: Matching mature-label pools and refit schedules
current_contribution_assessment.reason: The original frozen protocol and current methods explicitly control within-source completed labels and updates. This improves fairness but does not equalize feature lookbacks, local effective sample sizes, objective penalties or estimator families. Causal maturity is a necessary design requirement, not a new inference theorem.

current_contribution_assessment.claim: Negative source/model-family transport and retained failures
current_contribution_assessment.reason: Source-adapted, separately fitted specifications produce mixed FX results and many adverse Treasury/aggregate outcomes. They show fragility of executed procedures, not a causal mechanism or impossibility result for conditional methods. Numerical NA cells limit menu coverage and are not measured predictive losses.

current_contribution_assessment.claim: Score, breach counts, coherence and preference rankings can disagree
current_contribution_assessment.reason: Complete existing comparisons document this distinction on measured financial tasks. The general distinction between a proper score, exact breach frequency, shape constraints and decision costs is established; these recorded examples and matched comparisons are the applied evidence.

current_contribution_assessment.claim: Elementary finite geometry and classical Levy corollary
current_contribution_assessment.reason: Projection/order-statistic stability, coherent counterexamples, triangle inequality and an acknowledged classical maximal inequality explain constructions. The corrected AR simulations distinguish levels from increments and retain uncertainty; they do not create a new coverage theorem or financial validation.

current_contribution_assessment.reason: Twelve eligible series and two metadata/calendar skips broaden measured aggregate tasks, while shared dealers, categories, dates and reporting regimes prevent an independent-institution interpretation. No compatible unseen dealer has been added.

quality_judgment: The substantive contribution remains a bounded controlled application and model-validation benchmark with informative adverse evidence. Better chronology, mature comparators, exact numerical receipts, broader aggregate tasks and correction of mechanism mistakes strengthen credibility. They do not establish a new estimator, first financial peak forecast, general conditional advantage, fresh compatible dealer validation or measured financing/hedging benefit.
publication_boundary: No journal tier, acceptance probability or publication outcome is guaranteed. Usefulness and sufficient originality would depend on the specific venue and on whether the measured-position task, controlled comparisons and negative findings answer a consequential applied question. Compatible new financial observations and a specified decision-linked evaluation address more consequential remaining gaps than page count, citation count or extra diagnostics alone.
